calls.head: In close against from distance
calls.body: On shots from in close, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Boston is one of the worst. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Stars to do more of their damage around the net.

calls.head: Where the Stars have the edge: the penalty kill
calls.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the penalty kill, and the Bruins are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

surprises.head: Dallas got the good looks
surprises.body: Dallas’s shots at 5-on-5 had an 8.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.4% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 25 games.

story.head: Rantanen bags a hat trick
paras: Matthew Poitras opened the scoring for the Bruins early in the first, but Mikko Rantanen tied it 1-1 for Dallas early in the second. James Hagens gave the Bruins the lead less than five minutes later. Rantanen struck again late in the third to tie it 2-2. Rantanen completed his hat trick to win it on the power play in overtime.
The Stars had the better of the chances, outshooting the Bruins 25-20. Jake Oettinger made 18 saves for the Stars, and Jeremy Swayman stopped 22 of 25.
The Stars killed all four Bruins power plays. The Stars improved to 5-3-1, and the Bruins dropped to 7-2-1.

items.text: The Bruins’ five-game heater is over.
Three straight wins for the Stars.
David Pastrňák’s six-game point streak against Dallas ended.
Jason Robertson extended his point streak against Boston to seven games.
